paper_metadata.title: Design of a Blockchain-Driven Quantum Identity Model Using QHA-AC FQET and RL-QIDA Methods in Cloud Microservices
paper_metadata.venue: First International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Systems at the Edge (ICEdge)

summary: Blockchain-driven quantum-resistant identity verification framework for microservice-to-microservice authentication in financial cloud infrastructures. Integrates five components: Quantum Hash Anchoring with Adaptive Commitments (QHA-AC, using quantum random walks for temporally evolving hashes), Federated Quantum Entangled Tokens (FQET), Temporal Blockchain Quantum Graph Signatures (TBQGS), Quantum Zero-Knowledge Identity Tree (QZKIT), and Reinforcement-Learning-based Quantum Identity Drift Analysis (RL-QIDA). Evaluated on three datasets (FINStack-Micro, MS-FinBench, CloudAuthSim-Q) against three baseline methods. Reports identity-spoofing detection accuracy 94.5-97.2%, authentication latency 0.96-1.12 ms, drift detection 91.8-94.6%, privacy leakage 0.39-0.47%, consensus timestamp 11.8-12.6 ms. Quantum-entropy simulated on IBM Qiskit; no qubit counts or circuit specifications reported.

experiments.description: End-to-end evaluation of the QHA-AC / FQET / TBQGS / QZKIT / RL-QIDA framework on three microservice-identity datasets: FINStack-Micro, MS-FinBench, and the custom @CloudAuthSim-Q simulation dataset (1000 service identity traces with randomized DRL agents). Hybrid testbed: 10 virtual microservice nodes, quantum-entropy simulations on IBM Qiskit backends, blockchain layer on Hyperledger Fabric, Docker-containerized identity components. Performance compared against three reference methods (Method [3], Method [8], Method [12]) on spoofing-detection accuracy, authentication latency, and drift-detection accuracy (Tables I-III).

algorithm.variant: Five-component framework: QHA-AC (quantum random walk hashing + adaptive commitments), FQET (federated quantum entangled tokens), TBQGS (temporal blockchain quantum graph signatures), QZKIT (quantum zero-knowledge identity Merkle tree), RL-QIDA (DRL-based quantum identity drift analysis).
algorithm.ansatz: Quantum random walks generate temporally evolving identity hashes for QHA-AC; entangled key-pair generation for FQET across zones. No explicit gate-level ansatz or circuit description provided.
algorithm.optimizer: Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents used in RL-QIDA for drift detection and trust recalibration; specific DRL algorithm (DQN/PPO/etc.) not reported.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Identity state encoded as quantum-hash anchors produced by quantum random walks (QHA-AC) and committed on-chain; entangled token pairs distributed across zones (FQET); service-behavior graphs summarized by TBQGS signatures; identity attributes validated via a zero-knowledge Merkle tree (QZKIT).
problem_formulation.constraints: Quantum-resistance requirement; microservice latency budgets; blockchain consensus participation.

dataset_specification.description: FINStack-Micro and MS-FinBench: real-time service logs from open-source financial microservices including metadata, authentication traces, and performance metrics. CloudAuthSim-Q: custom simulation of authentication, drift, and entropy fluctuations across 1000 service identity traces using randomized DRL agents.
dataset_specification.notes: 1000 identity traces for the CloudAuthSim-Q subset; sizes of FINStack-Micro and MS-FinBench not reported.
